Statement of the problem: A 14-storey building in Bonifacio Global City (BGC), Taguig – a dense urban district with premium developments, strict zoning and heavy pedestrian activity. It integrates retail, a lobby, assembly spaces, office floors and a rooftop bar on a 2,000 m² floor plate. The uses must be zoned vertically so the ground-floor retail, second-floor function hall, office floors and rooftop bar operate independently yet cohesively. The office floors alone must achieve 70% efficiency. The design must also respond to BGC's urban interface: active frontage, pedestrian movement, vehicular access and service loading.

Program:
• Floor plate = 2,000 m²
• Ground floor: lobby (50%) with retail stores (50%)
• Second floor: 300-pax function hall, conference room and 6-pax meeting room (70% leasable)
• Third floor and above: offices at 70% efficiency, turned over to tenants in warm-shell condition
• Rooftop: restobar occupying 50% of the floor plate

Design objectives: clear vertical zoning and circulation; a compact core that keeps the offices at 70% efficiency; a safe, code-compliant assembly level (occupant load, exit widths, fire and life safety, circulation independent of retail and office traffic); a rooftop bar that is structurally feasible, acoustically controlled and served by dedicated service routes; response to the BGC context; a unified premium identity with sustainable, durable materials and energy-efficient systems.

q: For Project No. 2, all required parking slots will be located in the basement. Each basement level can accommodate 60 parking slots based on the structural grid and circulation layout. Given the total parking requirement of the project, how many basement levels are needed to provide the required number of parking slots?
n: Total demand is about 10 (retail) + 168 (offices) + 35 (bar) + the function hall's share, roughly 220 slots. At 60 per level, 220 ÷ 60 ≈ 3.7, so 4 basement levels. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Sec. 707; design brief.

PROJECT NO. 3 – SOCIALIZED HOUSING CONDOMINIUM

Statement of the problem: The City Government of Manila will develop eight (8) seven-storey socialized housing condominium buildings in Tondo under the Pambansang Pabahay Para sa Pilipino (4PH) program, for local government employees, minimum-wage earners and informal settler families. Each building has double-loaded corridors, 60 units per floor and 4-meter-wide dwelling modules, on a water-logged site.

Site: a 4-hectare water-logged property in Tondo, Manila; 8 buildings × 7 storeys; 60 units per floor along double-loaded corridors; 4-m unit frontage.

Design objectives: safe, affordable, dignified housing per 4PH; compact high-density development with adequate open space and community facilities; foundations and systems suited to a water-logged site (flood mitigation, soil improvement, durability); efficient double-loaded corridors and egress per the Fire Code and BP 220; natural ventilation, daylight and privacy in the 4-m modules; community facilities; cost-efficient modular construction; compliance with BP 220, the NBC, the Fire Code and Manila LGU guidelines.

q: In the hot-humid climate of the Philippines, which of the following provides the most effective passive cooling strategy for residential buildings?
n: Cross-ventilation with proper shading is the most effective passive cooling in hot-humid climates. Moving air cools by evaporation, and shading blocks heat gain. Source: Koenigsberger et al., Manual of Tropical Housing and Building; Givoni.
